name: biomolecules

phase_0.boundary_condition: cell membrane maintains biomolecular integrity while allowing selective transport

VINIT.chosen_element: primordial molecular chaos before biochemical organization
VINIT.justification: the initial unstructured state before biomolecular recognition

TANCH.chosen_element: cell membrane boundary that contains and protects biomolecule
TANCH.justification: the terminal boundary that defines the biomolecular operating environment

AFWD.chosen_element: anabolic synthesis reactions building complex molecules
AFWD.justification: forward morphism representing biosynthetic pathways creating biomolecules

AREV.chosen_element: catabolic degradation reactions breaking down molecules
AREV.justification: reverse transformation representing biomolecular breakdown and recycling

CLINK.chosen_element: covalent bonds linking atoms into functional biomolecules
CLINK.justification: composition connecting molecular subunits into larger structures

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: enzyme active sites recognizing specific substrates
IMSCRIB.justification: self-reference mechanism enabling biomolecular recognition and catalysis

FSPLIT.chosen_element: DNA transcription splitting double helix into mRNA
FSPLIT.justification: branching into template strand and coding strand for protein synthesis

FFUSE.chosen_element: ribosome fusing amino acids back into protein
FFUSE.justification: reconstitution of functional protein from individual amino acids

EVALF.chosen_element: failed binding due to conformational mismatch
EVALF.justification: negative evaluation preventing incorrect biomolecular reaction

ENGAGR.chosen_element: prion protein existing in both folded and misfolded states simultaneously
ENGAGR.justification: paraconsistency maintaining both native and pathological conformations

IFIX.chosen_element: genetic mutation permanently recorded in DNA sequence
IFIX.justification: irreversible recording of evolutionary biomolecular change

phase_3.void_description: pre-biotic chemical mixture before organized biomolecular function
phase_3.both_description: biomolecule maintaining both active and inactive conformations simultaneously

phase_5.compiler_frontend: ribosomes translating mRNA into proteins according to genetic code
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: signaling cascades and molecular transport across membranes
phase_5.memory_mechanism: DNA storing hereditary information and epigenetic modifications
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: circadian rhythms and enzyme kinetics controlling reaction timing

phase_6.cycle_cost: ATP hydrolysis and other high-energy bond breaking
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: substrates in higher energy configuration before enzyme action
phase_6.post_cycle_state: products released with energy dissipated as heat and work done
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — biomolecular processes couple energy-releasing and energy-consuming reactions
